intro_cards.title: About these notes
body: 8 units · tectonics to contours

Grade 12 is “geography of Eritrea in depth”. Grade 11 is the toolkit: how the crust moves, how water and wind carve, how people settle, then a first look at Eritrea’s place, relief and contour maps. Read each unit as a *story with a cause* — examiners mark the cause, not only the landform name.

intro_cards.title: Worked contour gradient
body: Two points: 1 200 m and 1 000 m. Map distance between them is 4 cm. Scale 1:50 000 (1 cm = 500 m).
Rise = 200 m. Run = 4 × 500 = 2 000 m. Gradient = 200/2000 = 1 in 10 (or 10%). Write both the fraction and a sentence: “For every 10 m walked horizontally you climb 1 m.”

units.title: Geographic Position, Shape and Size of Eritrea

cards.title: 6.1 Location
body: The relative location of Eritrea with respect to its neighboring, countries, water bodies and land masses.
The location of Eritrea can be expressed both in terms of the absolute and relative locations.
The absolute location is based on mathematical values, arc of circle, as well as imaginary lines of latitudes and longitudes.
The relative location of a place is determined by its location in relation to its nearby land masses and water bodies.
In terms of latitude, Eritrea extends from 12°42’ N (on the Djibouti border) to 18°02 N (Ras Kassar on the Sudan border).

cards.title: Where, how big, why it matters
body: Eritrea sits on the northern Horn of Africa, with a long **Red Sea** frontage. Neighbours: Sudan (west), Ethiopia (south), Djibouti (south-east). Latitude is tropical, so lowlands are hot; the plateau is liveable because **altitude** lowers temperature. Always mention both latitude and altitude when you explain climate here.

cards.title: Location of Eritrea
head: Type of location
Fact

From 36°25′ E (eastern Sudan border) to 43°10′ E (Red Sea shore at the Djibouti border)

body: Absolute location uses lines of latitude and longitude. Relative location describes a place by the land masses and water bodies around it.

cards.title: Location of Eritrea
body: Eritrea is in the **Horn of Africa**, in the Northern and Eastern hemispheres, roughly between latitudes 12°N and 18°N and longitudes 36°E and 43°E. It borders **Sudan** to the west, **Ethiopia** to the south and **Djibouti** to the south-east, and has a long coastline (about 1,200 km on the mainland) along the **Red Sea** to the east, including the **Dahlak archipelago**. Its position on the Red Sea, near the Bab el-Mandeb strait, gives it strategic importance for trade.

cards.title: Describe Eritrea's absolute and relative location
cards.problem: Describe the location of Eritrea (a) in absolute terms and (b) in relative terms.

steps.text: **Step 1: Absolute location uses latitude and longitude.** Eritrea extends from about 12°42′N (Djibouti border) to 18°02′N (Ras Kassar), and from about 36°25′E to 43°10′E.
**Step 2: Relative location uses neighbours and water bodies.** Red Sea to the east, Djibouti to the south-east, Ethiopia to the south and west, Sudan to the north and north-west.
**Step 3: Add the coast.** About 1,216 km of Red Sea coastline with the ports of Massawa and Assab.
**Step 4: Wider setting.** In the Horn of Africa, close to the Indian Ocean and the Mediterranean via the Red Sea.

cards.answer: (a) About 12°42′N–18°02′N and 36°25′E–43°10′E; (b) on the Red Sea in the Horn of Africa, bordered by Sudan, Ethiopia and Djibouti, with a 1,216 km coast and the ports of Massawa and Assab.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The absolute location of a place is given by ____.
cards.why:
**Step 1:** Absolute location uses the grid of latitude and longitude.

**Step 2:** It gives a single exact position on the globe.

**Step 3:** Neighbours and water bodies describe relative location.

**Tip:** Read the contour values first (do they rise or fall?), then the spacing (close = steep, wide = gentle) and the shape (V up = valley, V down = spur).

cards.why:
**Step 1:** Eritrea's neighbours: Sudan (north and west), Ethiopia (south and west), Djibouti (south-east).

**Step 2:** Yemen lies across the Red Sea, not on a land border.

**Step 3:** So the south-eastern neighbour is Djibouti.

**Tip:** Read the contour values first (do they rise or fall?), then the spacing (close = steep, wide = gentle) and the shape (V up = valley, V down = spur).

**Step 2:** The main ports on it are Massawa and Assab.

**Step 3:** The other values are far too short or too long.

**Tip:** Read the contour values first (do they rise or fall?), then the spacing (close = steep, wide = gentle) and the shape (V up = valley, V down = spur).

cards.title: 6.2 Administration
body: The six administrative zones are divided into 59 sub-zones.
All the remaining zones except the Southern Red Sea have common boundaries with it.
Asmara, the capital city of Eritrea is also found in this zone.
Five zones have common boundaries either with Sudan or Ethiopia.

cards.title: Administration
body: Eritrea is divided into six administrative regions (**zobas**): Maekel (Central, capital Asmara), Anseba, Gash-Barka, Debub (Southern), Semenawi Keyih Bahri (Northern Red Sea) and Debubawi Keyih Bahri (Southern Red Sea). Each zoba is divided into sub-zobas.

head: Zone
Centre
Area (km²)
Sub-zones
body: Maekel is the smallest zone and Gash-Barka the largest. Each sub-zone is divided into smaller units called kebabis. The whole coastline, with all ports and islands, belongs to the Northern and Southern Red Sea zones.

cards.title: Zones, sub-zones and kebabis
body: Eritrea is divided into **six administrative zones (zobas)**: Maekel, Debub, Anseba, Gash-Barka, Northern Red Sea and Southern Red Sea. These are divided into **59 sub-zones**, and each sub-zone into smaller units called **kebabis**.
**Maekel** (centre: Asmara) is the smallest zone (about 1,400 km², 7 sub-zones) but the most densely populated. Every zone except the Southern Red Sea borders it.

**Gash-Barka** (Barentu) is the largest (about 34,500 km², 14 sub-zones), followed by the Northern Red Sea (Massawa, about 33,200 km²), the Southern Red Sea (Assab, about 23,400 km², 4 sub-zones), Anseba (Keren, about 22,100 km²) and Debub (Mendefera, about 9,700 km², 14 sub-zones).
The whole coastline, with all the ports, harbours and islands, belongs to the Northern and Southern Red Sea zones: Massawa is in the north and Assab in the south. Five zones border Sudan or Ethiopia.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which one of the following Zones has **no** common boundary with **Zoba Maekel**?
cards.why: **Zoba Maekel** (Central Region) is landlocked in the center of Eritrea. It is bordered by Anseba, Gash-Barka, and Debub. It does **not** touch the **Southern Red Sea** zone, which is located far to the southeast.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: How many regions of Eritrea have common boundaries with Ethiopia?
cards.why: Three administrative regions of Eritrea share a border with Ethiopia: Gash-Barka, Debub (Southern), and Southern Red Sea (Debubawi Qeih Bahri).

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: One of the following administrative zones has the **least** number of sub-zones.
cards.why: The Southern Red Sea region of Eritrea is divided into only 4 sub-zones (Assab, Central Denkalya, Southern Denkalya, and Are'eta). This is the lowest count among the administrative regions due to its low population density and large arid areas. Maekel has 6 sub-zones.

lessons.title: The Size and Shape of Eritrea

cards.title: 6.3 The Size and Shape of Eritrea
body: Eritrea has a total area of 124,330 square kilometers.
Eritrea also possesses over 360 islands, which have a total coastline of over 1258.4 kilometers.
The islands can be generally classified into small or large islands on the basis of the total area they occupy.
Small islands occupy less than 10 square kilometer each.
The largest island is called **Dahlak Kebir**.

cards.title: Where, how big, why it matters
body: The country is elongated roughly north–south, thin in places, with the Dahlak waters and a southern Red Sea reach. That shape gives a long coast relative to land area — useful for ports and fisheries, awkward for east–west roads that must climb the escarpment.

cards.title: Islands, bays and gulfs
body: Eritrea covers **124,330 km²**. It is roughly triangular: wide in the north-west and narrowing towards the south-east along the Red Sea. About 80 sovereign states are smaller, so it is a medium-sized country.

It has **over 360 coral islands** with more than 1,258 km of coastline. **Small islands** (under 10 km² each) number about 339 and together cover only about 233 km²; the **15 large islands** (over 10 km² each) cover about 1,101 km².

**Dahlak Kebir** (about 643 km²) is the largest island – bigger than countries such as the Seychelles or Malta – followed by **Norah** (about 103 km²) and **Halba**. Most islands lie east of Massawa and north of the Buri Peninsula; others are in the Gulf of Hawakil and the Gulf of Assab.
Only about ten islands have permanent villages; Dahlak Kebir has the most (8). South of Massawa the coast is indented with bays and gulfs: Hirgigo, Zula, Hawakil, Anfile, Beilul and Assab.

cards.title: Describe the size and shape of Eritrea
cards.problem: Describe the size and shape of Eritrea and explain one advantage and one disadvantage of its shape.

steps.text: **Step 1: Size.** Total area 124,330 km² – neither very small nor very large (about 80 countries are smaller).
**Step 2: Shape.** Roughly triangular: wide in the north-west, narrowing to the south-east along the Red Sea, with over 360 islands offshore.
**Step 3: Advantage.** A long coastline (over 1,200 km on the mainland) relative to its area gives access to ports, fishing and sea trade.
**Step 4: Disadvantage.** The long, narrow south-east makes it far and costly to connect places such as Assab with the centre by road.
**Conclusion:** a medium-sized, triangular country with a long coast.

cards.answer: About 124,330 km², roughly triangular and narrowing to the south-east; the long coast helps ports and fishing, but the narrow south-east is hard to link to the centre.

cards.title: 6.4 Strategic Position of Eritrea
body: The geographical location of a country, which is expressed through its absolute and relative locations, is closely associated with the country’s natural resources endowments as well.
The strategic position of the country is. therefore. best explained in relation to its relative and absolute geographical locations.
Eritrea is not far from the equatorial location.
The Eritrean Red Sea coast stretches for about 1216 kilometers along the western shore of the Red Sea.
Most commercial lines directed to Europe and the Mediterranean regions from the Persian Gulf, East Africa and Asia pass through the Red Sea.

cards.title: Where, how big, why it matters
body: **Strategic position:** the Red Sea is a world shortcut between the Mediterranean / Suez and the Indian Ocean. A state that can offer a safe port on that lane has diplomatic and commercial weight out of proportion to its land size. Internally the Massawa–Asmara corridor ties the sea to the populated highlands. Assab sits further south on the same sea.

cards.title: Why Eritrea's position is strategic
body: A country's **strategic position** is the importance it gains from its absolute location (latitude and longitude) and relative location (its position compared with seas, routes and neighbours).
**Absolute location:** Eritrea lies roughly between 12°N and 18°N and between 36°E and 43°E, in the Horn of Africa, not far north of the equator.

**Relative location:** its mainland coast runs for about 1,200 km along the western shore of the **Red Sea**, between the Suez Canal in the north and the strait of **Bab el-Mandeb** in the south – the gateway to the Gulf of Aden and the Indian Ocean. Much of the shipping between Europe and the Persian Gulf, East Africa and Asia passes along this route.

It is also a **transition zone** between tropical Africa and the Arabian Peninsula. Coastal trading stations served merchants, missionaries and invaders, and this is why Turks, Egyptians, Italians, the British and Ethiopians all sought control of the territory.
Other Red Sea states: Sudan, Egypt, Djibouti, Yemen and Saudi Arabia; Israel and Jordan reach it through the Gulf of Aqaba.

cards.title: Explain the strategic importance of Eritrea
cards.problem: Using absolute and relative location, explain why Eritrea has a strategic position.

steps.text: **Step 1: Absolute location.** Between about 12°–18°N and 36°–43°E, in the Horn of Africa.
**Step 2: Relative location.** A long Red Sea coast between the Suez Canal and Bab el-Mandeb.
**Step 3: Trade route.** Ships between Europe and Asia, the Persian Gulf and East Africa pass along this coast, so ports such as Massawa and Assab can serve and influence world trade.
**Step 4: Crossroads.** It links tropical Africa with Arabia, which is why many foreign powers wanted to control it.
**Conclusion:** its position on a world sea lane and at a continental crossroads makes it strategic.

cards.answer: It lies in the Horn of Africa on a long Red Sea coast between Suez and Bab el-Mandeb, beside a major world shipping route and at the crossroads of Africa and Arabia.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which strait at the southern end of the Red Sea makes Eritrea's coast strategically important?
cards.why:
**Step 1:** The Red Sea opens to the Gulf of Aden and the Indian Ocean through the Bab el-Mandeb strait.

**Step 2:** Eritrea's southern coast (near Assab) is close to this strait.

**Step 3:** Gibraltar, Hormuz and the Bosporus are elsewhere.

**Tip:** Read every option against the rule before choosing.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The strategic position of a country is best explained using its ____.
cards.why:
**Step 1:** Absolute location gives latitude and longitude.

**Step 2:** Relative location gives its position compared with seas, routes and neighbours.

**Step 3:** Together they explain why the location matters.

**Tip:** Read every option against the rule before choosing.

cards.q: Why did many foreign powers want to control Eritrea in the past?

options.B: Its oil fields in the highlands
options.D: Its Red Sea coast and position between Africa and Arabia

cards.why:
**Step 1:** The Red Sea coast offered ports on an important trade route.

**Step 2:** Eritrea is a crossing point between tropical Africa and Arabia.

**Step 3:** It has no snowfields, is medium-sized, and has no highland oil fields.
